Aatrox.combo: For a basic trade, attack with Quinn P Harrier's mark to gain Quinn W Heightened Senses' attack speed and movement speed, land one or two more attacks, then knock Aatrox back with Quinn E Vault and retreat. When Aatrox E Umbral Dash is down and you can all-in, use Quinn E Vault to engage, then an empowered attack, Quinn Q Blinding Assault, and follow-up attacks. Use Quinn Q Blinding Assault when Aatrox is outside the minion line so a minion doesn't get hit first.
Aatrox.laning: When Aatrox steps up to last-hit, poke with an attack marked by Quinn P Harrier, then immediately back off. Farm without giving up an early kill, and use the mark for short trades with Aatrox instead of wasting it on minions. Push the wave under his turret, then use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to create a numbers advantage in another lane or the enemy jungle.
Aatrox.fight: Trade briefly just after Aatrox uses the empowered attack from Aatrox P Deathbringer Stance on a minion. Avoid the edge of Aatrox Q The Darkin Blade, and don't accept a duel during Aatrox R World Ender even if you have equal health. Look to engage after Aatrox E Umbral Dash is down.
Aatrox.teamfight: Don't engage from the front; finish off targets already caught from the side or behind. Save Quinn E Vault to knock away enemies who get on you and escape. You can push the opposite side lane and join with Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines, so rotate early if your team can't hold its position.
Aatrox.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Aatrox Q The Darkin Blade and Aatrox W Infernal Chains. If healing lets him shrug off your poke, slot Executioner's Calling between core items. Add penetration because Aatrox's high armor blocks Quinn's main source of physical damage.
Aatrox.escape: If Aatrox W Infernal Chains hits you, move out of its area immediately and use the Quinn E Vault you've saved if needed. Look for an engage immediately after you force Aatrox to use E Umbral Dash. If Aatrox uses a mobility spell to move deeper into his team, Quinn E Vault will follow him and land there too, so first check whether your allies can follow.
Aatrox.phase: Quinn's role in frontal teamfights diminishes in the late game, so use side-lane pressure.
Aatrox.watch: Aatrox Q The Darkin Blade is dangerous if its blade edge hits you, so watch the cast and dodge outside its edge or toward the inner area. If Aatrox W Infernal Chains hits you, leave its area immediately before it pulls you in, and save Quinn E Vault for this moment. When Aatrox R World Ender is active, his attack damage and healing increase, so avoid dueling and create distance.

Kled.watch: If Kled Q Bear Trap on a Rope hits you, create distance before it pulls you in. When Kled W Violent Tendencies is active, use Quinn E Vault to knock him back and disengage before he lands his fourth attack. Also watch for Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! starting out of vision.
Kled.build: Build armor first against Kled’s main damage from Kled Q Bear Trap on a Rope, Kled W Violent Tendencies, and Kled E Jousting. Armor won’t block the magic damage from Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!!. Kled W Violent Tendencies and Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! deal damage based on your maximum health, so be careful about stacking health alone.
Kled.combo: If Kled’s mobility and pull threat are down and you can safely engage, attack in this order: Quinn E Vault → empowered attack on the mark → Quinn Q Blinding Assault → basic attack. Consuming the mark from Quinn E Vault right away grants the attack speed and movement speed from Quinn W Heightened Senses.
Kled.escape: Look to engage after the pull threat from Kled Q Bear Trap on a Rope is gone and both Kled E Jousting and Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! are down. If Kled can move into the enemy backline with E or R, Quinn E Vault follows him and lands you there too, so don’t rush in when only one mobility spell is down.
Kled.fight: When Kled steps up to last-hit, use a Quinn P Harrier-marked basic attack to gain the attack speed and movement speed from Quinn W Heightened Senses, then land one or two more attacks and back off. If Kled closes in to retaliate or activates Kled W Violent Tendencies, knock him back with Quinn E Vault to end the short trade.
Kled.laning: Use your ranged advantage to briefly poke with a marked basic attack whenever Kled steps up to last-hit. Quinn Q Blinding Assault won’t leave a mark on Kled if it hits a minion first, so use it when he steps outside the minion line. If you can’t finish Kled after he dismounts Skaarl, create distance. In lane, push him away from minions so he can’t build Courage by farming.
Kled.phase: Quinn has less impact in front-to-back teamfights later, so keep applying side-lane pressure.
Kled.teamfight: Secure vision on the flanks because Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! can come from out of vision. Don’t engage from the front; approach from the side or behind to finish targets who are already caught, and save Quinn E Vault to knock away enemies who get on you and escape. If your allies can hold, push the opposite side lane; if the fight is about to collapse, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to join early.

Aurora.escape: Don't engage just because Aurora W Across the Veil is down; check whether she can still use Aurora E The Weirding and Aurora R Between Worlds. In particular, use Quinn E Vault to engage before Aurora R Between Worlds comes off cooldown, only when her remaining mobility is down or your allies can follow. If Aurora uses a mobility spell to move deeper into her team, Quinn E Vault follows her too, so check where you will land first.
Aurora.build: If Aurora P Spirit Abjuration's healing blunts your brief poke, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Aurora's main damage is magic, so prioritize magic resistance over armor.
Aurora.combo: For a safe trade, use an empowered attack against a target marked by Quinn P Harrier, then an additional attack while benefiting from Quinn W Heightened Senses' passive, followed by Quinn E Vault. When Aurora's mobility spells are down and you can all-in, use Quinn E Vault, an empowered attack, Quinn Q Blinding Assault, then an attack.
Aurora.fight: When Quinn P Harrier marks Aurora, use an empowered attack to gain Quinn W Heightened Senses' attack speed and movement speed, land one or two more attacks, then knock her back with Quinn E Vault and retreat. During Aurora W Across the Veil's stealth, wait until she is revealed. If affected by Aurora Q Twofold Hex and health has decreased, end the trade.
Aurora.laning: Don't waste Quinn P Harrier's mark on a minion; trade briefly when Aurora is marked. Quinn Q Blinding Assault won't mark Aurora if it hits a minion first, so cast it when she steps outside the minion line. Push the wave under her turret, then use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to create a numbers advantage in another lane or the enemy jungle.
Aurora.phase: Quinn is strong from the start with mark-based poke and is strongest in the mid game after her first core item. Her role in frontal teamfights diminishes in the late game, so pressure side lanes.
Aurora.teamfight: Avoid engaging from the front; finish only targets already caught from the side or behind, and save Quinn E Vault to knock away enemies who get on you and escape. If Aurora jumps in and fails to secure a takedown, look for a chance to punish her. When an ally dies, Aurora's jump cooldown resets, so don't leave low-health allies behind as you retreat.
Aurora.watch: If Aurora Q Twofold Hex hits you, move off the line between you and Aurora before the curse is pulled back. The return damage scales with your missing health, so retreat sooner when your health is low. Aurora R Between Worlds slows you when you leave its area, so decide whether to get out before it forms.

Olaf.phase: Olaf is strong early, so use your range advantage for brief harass without getting caught and killed. After gaining Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines, Quinn can use her mobility to affect other lanes, and she peaks in the mid game after her first core item. Olaf is relatively weaker late, but Quinn also has a smaller role in head-on teamfights, so use side-lane pressure.
Olaf.build: Build armor first against Olaf Q Undertow and his basic attacks. Olaf E Reckless Swing deals true damage, so counter it with health and spacing rather than resistances. If Olaf’s basic attacks are a concern, consider reducing his attack speed.
Olaf.combo: Start short trades with a basic attack on a Quinn P Harrier-marked target, add one or two more basic attacks empowered by Quinn W Heightened Senses, then knock Olaf back with Quinn E Vault to end the trade. When you have an opening to engage, attack in this order: Quinn E Vault → empowered basic attack on a marked target → Quinn Q Blinding Assault → basic attack. Don’t attempt this engage combo while Olaf R Ragnarok is active.
Olaf.escape: Olaf has no ability to create distance on his own, so you can close in with Quinn E Vault once Olaf R Ragnarok ends and a safe engage angle opens. First, limit his approach path by preventing him from retrieving the Olaf Q Undertow axe, and make sure the landing spot for Quinn E Vault isn’t dangerous.
Olaf.fight: When Olaf steps up to last-hit, briefly harass him with a basic attack on a Quinn P Harrier-marked target, then retreat using the attack speed and movement speed from Quinn W Heightened Senses. If he closes in to retaliate, knock him back with Quinn E Vault, but focus on creating distance while Olaf R Ragnarok is active. Don’t stay close and fight for long even as Olaf’s health decreases, since his attack speed and healing become stronger.
Olaf.laning: Use your range to land a marked basic attack only when Olaf steps forward to last-hit, then retreat. Move away from where Olaf Q Undertow’s axe lands to make it harder for him to retrieve it and close in again. Avoid giving up an early kill while pushing the wave, then use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to create a numbers advantage elsewhere.
Olaf.teamfight: Don’t engage from the front; clean up targets who are already caught from the flank. Save Quinn E Vault to knock back enemies who close in and escape, and create distance to wait out Olaf R Ragnarok if it’s active. Push the opposite side lane if your team can hold; if the fight is about to collapse, join early with Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines.
Olaf.watch: Watch for Olaf Q Undertow’s slow and armor reduction, and move away from where the axe lands to prevent him from retrieving it. When Olaf R Ragnarok is active, don’t try to stop him with Quinn E Vault; create distance instead. Hitting him with Quinn E Vault or a basic attack during this time may extend Olaf R Ragnarok’s duration.

Camille.build: Build armor first against Camille's main damage. Camille Q Precision Protocol's true damage can't be reduced by armor, and Camille W Tactical Sweep scales with your maximum health, so be careful about stacking health alone. If Camille W Tactical Sweep's healing makes your poke ineffective, buy Executioner's Calling between core items.
Camille.combo: When you have a safe opening to engage, use Quinn E Vault, an empowered attack immediately after landing, Quinn Q Blinding Assault, then an attack. If you consume the mark left by Quinn E Vault with an attack, you also gain Quinn W Heightened Senses' attack speed and movement speed. If Camille still has a mobility spell, check before engaging because Quinn E Vault can follow her deep into her team.
Camille.escape: Look for an opening when both Camille E Hookshot and Camille R The Hextech Ultimatum are down. In particular, you can close the gap with Quinn E Vault before Camille R The Hextech Ultimatum comes back. Also check whether your allies are close enough to follow.
Camille.fight: Avoid trading right after Camille P Adaptive Defenses activates its shield. When P Harrier marks her, use an empowered attack to gain Quinn W Heightened Senses' attack speed and movement speed, land more attacks, then knock her back with Quinn E Vault and retreat. If Camille Q Precision Protocol's empowered attack threatens you, land Quinn Q Blinding Assault or create distance.
Camille.laning: Early on, poke briefly with a marked attack when Camille steps up to last-hit. Stay away from walls, and use Quinn Q Blinding Assault when she is outside the minion line. Take lane control before Camille gets her first core item, then shove the wave in and use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to impact another area.
Camille.phase: Early on, Quinn's mark-based poke is strong and Camille is weak before her first core item, so pressure her farming. In the mid game after the first core item is completed, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to push lanes and join allies elsewhere for an advantage. Late game, Quinn's role in head-on teamfights falls off, so pressure side lanes, but don't leave Camille alone in a side lane for long.
Camille.teamfight: Don't engage from the front; finish targets already caught from the side or behind. Save Quinn E Vault to knock Camille away and escape if she gets on you. If your team can hold, push the opposite side lane; if the fight is about to collapse, rotate early with Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines.
Camille.watch: Camille E Hookshot uses walls to engage from long range and stun you. Stand away from walls, and interrupt her dash with Quinn E Vault as soon as her hook catches a wall. Don't use a response ability at the moment Camille R The Hextech Ultimatum engages; if trapped, wait out the zone's duration, then counterattack.

Trundle.watch: If Trundle Q Chomp hits you, it lowers Quinn’s attack damage and makes trades unfavorable, so back off until the effect ends. Don’t fight inside Trundle W Frozen Domain; wait out its duration outside. When Trundle E Pillar of Ice appears, move sideways before the slow catches you. Keep your distance while Trundle R Subjugate is active.
Trundle.build: If Trundle P King's Tribute healing erases your harass, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Consider armor first against Trundle Q Chomp and his basic attacks, but Trundle R Subjugate reduces your resistances and deals damage based on your maximum health, so do not rely on adding only resistances or health.
Trundle.combo: For a short trade, start with an auto attack on Quinn P Harrier's mark, use the attack speed and movement speed from Quinn W Heightened Senses, then add one or two auto attacks and end by knocking him back with Quinn E Vault. If Trundle E Pillar of Ice is down and you can engage, follow with Quinn E Vault → empowered auto attack immediately after landing → Quinn Q Blinding Assault → auto attack. Use Quinn Q Blinding Assault when you have a clear line so a minion is not hit first.
Trundle.escape: Once Trundle E Pillar of Ice is down, there is less risk of the pillar blocking your escape, so look for an opening to engage. Trundle has no skill that creates distance on his own, but when engaging with Quinn E Vault, check your landing position and whether your allies can follow up. If the pillar is still available or you are in a narrow path, save Quinn E Vault to knock away Trundle when he is close and escape.
Trundle.fight: When Trundle comes forward to last-hit, briefly harass with an auto attack on Quinn P Harrier's mark. If he closes in to retaliate, knock him back with Quinn E Vault as you retreat. Break off the fight if you are hit by Trundle Q Chomp or Trundle W Frozen Domain is placed, then fight again once the unfavorable window passes. Before engaging, check that Trundle E Pillar of Ice is down and that you can land safely.
Trundle.laning: As a ranged champion, Quinn should land a marked auto attack whenever Trundle steps forward to last-hit, then immediately back off. Trundle can heal near the wave with Trundle P King's Tribute, so capitalize immediately after chipping him down, such as by pushing the lane to force him to recall. After pushing the wave into the enemy turret, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to influence another lane or the enemy jungle.
Trundle.phase: In the late game, Quinn's role in front-to-back teamfights shrinks, so choose when to apply side-lane pressure and when to join your team.
Trundle.teamfight: While Trundle R Subjugate is active, attack someone else or create distance from Trundle. Quinn should not engage head-on; clean up targets already caught out from the side or behind, and save Quinn E Vault to knock back a nearby enemy and escape. If you are pushing the opposite side lane, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to choose when to join, but join early if your team is about to collapse.

Urgot.fight: When Quinn P Harrier marks Urgot from outside his short attack range, use an empowered basic attack to poke briefly. If Urgot approaches with W Purge active, walk away to create distance, and don’t stay near him long enough to be hit by Urgot P Echoing Flames multiple times. Look for an angle to use Quinn E Vault to engage only after Urgot E Disdain is down.
Urgot.build: Urgot has fairly high armor, so consider armor penetration first to boost Quinn's physical damage. Urgot deals mainly physical damage, and Urgot P Echoing Flames deals damage based on your maximum health, so prioritize armor for resistance.
Urgot.combo: A standard trade goes: Quinn P Harrier marked basic attack → an extra basic attack with the passive from Quinn W Heightened Senses → Quinn E Vault to knock him back as you disengage. If Urgot E Disdain is down and it is safe to engage, attack with Quinn E Vault → empowered basic attack right after landing → Quinn Q Blinding Assault → basic attack.
Urgot.escape: Keep your distance and do not use Quinn E Vault to engage while Urgot E Disdain is available. Right after forcing Urgot to use E Disdain is your window to go in with Quinn E Vault. Use Quinn E Vault to disengage when Urgot Q Corrosive Charge hits and you need to get away.
Urgot.laning: When Urgot steps forward to last-hit, land a Quinn P Harrier marked basic attack and retreat outside his short range. Use Quinn Q Blinding Assault when Urgot steps outside the minion line so a minion does not block it first. Push the wave under Urgot's turret, then use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to move to another lane or into the enemy jungle.
Urgot.phase: Early on, Quinn can pressure Urgot with her range and Quinn P Harrier-mark poke. Once Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines is available, push the lane and create a numbers advantage elsewhere, making use of your strength in the mid game after your first core item. Later, Quinn has less of a role in front-to-back teamfights, so pressure a side lane and choose when to join your team.
Urgot.teamfight: Urgot E Disdain stops at the first champion hit, so position behind your frontline. Quinn should clean up targets already caught from the side instead of engaging from the front, and save Quinn E Vault as an escape to knock away enemies who get close. If your team can hold, push the opposite side lane; if the fight is about to collapse, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to join early.
Urgot.watch: Urgot E Disdain dashes in and then stuns, making it dangerous for Quinn, so do not use Quinn E Vault to engage before it is down. If Urgot Q Corrosive Charge hits you, its slow overlaps with the targeting from Urgot W Purge, so use Quinn E Vault to create distance. If Urgot R Fear Beyond Death hits you, get completely out of range before your health reaches the execute threshold.

Akali.build: Build magic resistance before armor because the damage from Akali P Assassin's Mark, Akali Q Five Point Strike, and Akali E Shuriken Flip is all magic damage. Get some health to withstand the second hit of Akali R Perfect Execution.
Akali.combo: For a short trade, use an empowered attack with P Harrier's mark to gain Quinn W Heightened Senses' attack speed and movement speed, land one or two more attacks, then end the trade by knocking Akali back with Quinn E Vault. When Akali's mobility spells are down and you can fight to the finish, use Quinn E Vault, an empowered attack immediately after landing, Quinn Q Blinding Assault, then an attack.
Akali.escape: Don't engage just because only one of Akali E Shuriken Flip or W Twilight Shroud is down. Use Quinn E Vault to close the gap before Akali R Perfect Execution comes back up, while her other mobility is also unavailable. If Akali uses a mobility spell to go deeper in, Quinn E Vault follows her, so check where you will land first.
Akali.fight: Look to use Quinn Q Blinding Assault during the brief moment Akali is revealed when entering Akali W Twilight Shroud. Before going in deep, check which of Akali W Twilight Shroud, Akali E Shuriken Flip, and Akali R Perfect Execution she still has available for mobility.
Akali.laning: When Akali steps up to last-hit, poke with an empowered attack marked by P Harrier, then immediately back off. Quinn Q Blinding Assault won't mark Akali if it hits a minion first, so use it when she steps outside the minion line. Push the wave under the enemy turret, then use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to join another lane or the enemy jungle.
Akali.phase: Quinn's role in frontal teamfights diminishes in the late game, so pressure side lanes.
Akali.teamfight: Quinn doesn't engage from the front; she finishes targets already caught from the side or behind. Save Quinn E Vault to knock Akali back and escape when she approaches. If your team can hold, push the opposite side lane; if the fight is about to collapse, rotate early with Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines.
Akali.watch: Once the mark is applied, the second dash follows Quinn, so if you've been marked, save Quinn E Vault and use it to knock the enemy back when they approach.

Chogath.build: If Cho'Gath P Carnivore's healing erases your poke, slot Executioner's Calling between core items. Consider magic resistance against the damage from Cho'Gath Q Rupture, W Feral Scream, and E Vorpal Spikes. Cho'Gath R Feast deals true damage, so magic resistance can't stop it.
Chogath.combo: For a short trade, use an attack marked by Quinn P Harrier, an extra attack with Quinn W Heightened Senses' passive active, then Quinn E Vault to knock him back and disengage. When you have a safe opening to get on him, use Quinn E Vault, a marked empowered attack, Quinn Q Blinding Assault, then an extra attack. Cast Quinn Q Blinding Assault when Cho'Gath is outside the minion line so it doesn't hit a minion first.
Chogath.escape: Cho'Gath has no mobility spells, so use Quinn E Vault to engage after Cho'Gath Q Rupture and W Feral Scream are down and you have a safe landing spot. If he uses Flash to move deeper into his team, Quinn E Vault follows him too, so check that possibility and whether your allies can follow before engaging. If silenced, walk out first instead of trying to cast a spell.
Chogath.fight: When Cho'Gath steps up to last-hit, poke briefly with an attack marked by Quinn P Harrier, then retreat using the attack speed and movement speed from Quinn W Heightened Senses. If he tries to get on you, knock him back with Quinn E Vault, but create distance before Cho'Gath W Feral Scream can silence you. Look to engage after Cho'Gath Q Rupture and W Feral Scream are down.
Chogath.laning: From early on, pressure melee Cho'Gath with a marked attack when he steps up to last-hit. Cho'Gath E Vorpal Spikes pierces minions, so stand off the line behind minions and away from the direction of his attacks. Pressure Cho'Gath's growth by pushing the wave, then use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines after pushing it in to create a numbers advantage elsewhere.
Chogath.phase: Early on, Quinn's mark-based poke is good for keeping Cho'Gath under pressure. As Cho'Gath builds stacks over time, the matchup turns against Quinn, so use side-lane pressure rather than relying on head-on teamfights late.
Chogath.teamfight: Quinn doesn't engage from the front where Cho'Gath is; she finishes targets already caught from the side or behind. Save Quinn E Vault to knock away enemies who get on you and escape, avoiding a landing in the middle of the enemy team after Cho'Gath's crowd control. If your team can hold, push the opposite side lane; if the fight is about to collapse, rotate early with Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines.
Chogath.watch: When the ground telegraph for Cho'Gath Q Rupture appears under your feet, immediately walk to the side to dodge it, using Quinn E Vault at that moment if needed. If Cho'Gath W Feral Scream silences you, you can't use Quinn E Vault, so avoid facing him head-on and walk out first. If your health is at or below half, keep your distance to guard against the true damage from Cho'Gath R Feast.

Darius.build: Build armor first against Darius P Hemorrhage, Darius Q Decimate, and Darius W Crippling Strike, his main sources of damage. However, armor has limited effect against the penetration on Darius E Apprehend and the true damage from Darius R Noxian Guillotine, so consider health too. If Darius Q Decimate's healing makes your poke pointless, slot Executioner's Calling between core items, and add penetration against Darius's high armor.
Darius.combo: For a short trade, use an attack marked by Quinn P Harrier to gain Quinn W Heightened Senses' attack speed and movement speed, land one or two more attacks, then end by knocking Darius back with Quinn E Vault. When Darius E Apprehend is down and you have an opening to engage, use Quinn E Vault, a marked attack immediately after landing, Quinn Q Blinding Assault, then an attack. Your landing spot depends on the direction you use Quinn E Vault, so first choose a safe direction to retreat.
Darius.escape: The window while Darius E Apprehend is down is your chance to close the gap with Quinn E Vault. If Darius E Apprehend is still available, save Quinn E Vault and Flash as responses, and immediately create distance if Darius P Hemorrhage stacks up.
Darius.fight: Trade briefly from outside Darius E Apprehend range, and look to trade just after Darius E Apprehend misses or he uses Darius Q Decimate to clear minions. Avoid extended fights because of Darius Q Decimate's healing and Darius P Hemorrhage stacks. Before using Quinn E Vault to engage, check whether Darius R Noxian Guillotine is down and your allies can follow.
Darius.laning: When Darius steps forward to last-hit, poke with an attack marked by Quinn P Harrier, then immediately back off. Use Quinn Q Blinding Assault when Darius is outside the minion line so a minion doesn't get hit first. Push the wave under Darius's turret, then use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to create a numbers advantage in another lane or the enemy jungle.
Darius.phase: Quinn's role in head-on teamfights falls off late, so play around side-lane pressure.
Darius.teamfight: Quinn doesn't engage from the front; she finishes only targets already caught from the side or behind. Save Quinn E Vault to knock away enemies who get on you and escape, and be careful not to land in the middle of the enemy team while following Darius R Noxian Guillotine. If you push the opposite side lane and your team is about to collapse, rotate early with Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines.
Darius.watch: If Darius E Apprehend pulls you in, an attack, Darius W Crippling Strike, and Darius Q Decimate will follow, so poke from outside E range. When you see Darius Q Decimate, get out of the blade's range to deny its healing. If Darius P Hemorrhage stacks up, create distance to drop the stacks, and don't remain in range of Darius R Noxian Guillotine with multiple stacks on you.

DrMundo.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Dr. Mundo E Blunt Force Trauma. If healing from Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases, Q Infected Bonesaw, and W Heart Zapper erases your poke, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Also account for the magic damage from Dr. Mundo Q Infected Bonesaw and W Heart Zapper, which armor can't block.
DrMundo.combo: For a basic trade, use an attack marked by Quinn P Harrier to activate Quinn W Heightened Senses' passive, land one or two more attacks, then end by knocking him back with Quinn E Vault if Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases is down. To engage after Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases is down, use Quinn E Vault, an empowered attack immediately after landing, Quinn Q Blinding Assault, then an attack. If a minion is in front of Quinn Q Blinding Assault, it won't mark Dr. Mundo, so clear the line.
DrMundo.escape: Dr. Mundo has no spell to create distance himself, so look to engage when Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases is down and you have a clear line for Quinn Q Blinding Assault. Check minion positions so you can dodge the slow from Dr. Mundo Q Infected Bonesaw. Quinn E Vault follows its target even if they Flash, so don't use it to engage if you could end up deep in the enemy team.
DrMundo.fight: When Dr. Mundo steps up to last-hit, poke briefly with an attack marked by Quinn P Harrier, use the attack speed and movement speed from Quinn W Heightened Senses to land one or two more attacks, then retreat. When Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases is down, you can end the trade by knocking him back with Quinn E Vault. Don't spend time trying to kill him while Dr. Mundo R Maximum Dosage is active.
DrMundo.laning: Keep a minion between you and Dr. Mundo to block Dr. Mundo Q Infected Bonesaw, but look to use Quinn Q Blinding Assault when he steps outside the minion line. When Dr. Mundo is in trading range, save Quinn P Harrier's mark for him instead of using it on a minion. After trading, if the canister Dr. Mundo dropped is on your safe escape route, step on it to deny his healing and passive cooldown reduction.
DrMundo.phase: Early on, Quinn can pressure Dr. Mundo's last-hitting with her ranged attack range and Quinn P Harrier's mark-based poke. Quinn's role in head-on teamfights falls off late, so keep up side-lane pressure.
DrMundo.teamfight: Don't try to push through Dr. Mundo from the front; finish targets already caught from the side or behind. Save Quinn E Vault to knock away enemies who get on you and escape, and don't spend time chasing Dr. Mundo while Dr. Mundo R Maximum Dosage is active. If your team can hold, push the opposite side lane; if the fight is about to collapse, rotate early with Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines.
DrMundo.watch: Dr. Mundo Q Infected Bonesaw slows the first target hit and deals damage based on their current health, so be especially careful when your health is high and dodge from behind minions. If Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases is ready, it ignores the first immobilizing effect, so don't rely on Quinn E Vault's knockback to retreat. If Dr. Mundo R Maximum Dosage is active, stop chasing, taking his healing and movement speed into account.

Fiora.build: Build armor first against Fiora Q Lunge and Fiora E Bladework. Fiora P Duelist's Dance and Fiora R Grand Challenge deal true damage that armor can't block, and R damage also scales with your maximum health, so be careful about stacking health alone. If healing blunts your poke, buy Executioner's Calling between core items.
Fiora.combo: Start a short trade with an attack marked by Quinn P Harrier to gain Quinn W Heightened Senses' attack speed and movement speed, land one or two more attacks, then end by knocking Fiora back with Quinn E Vault. When Fiora Q Lunge and W Riposte are down and you can engage, use Quinn E Vault, a marked empowered attack, Quinn Q Blinding Assault, then an attack. Use Q when Fiora is outside the minion line so a minion doesn't get hit first.
Fiora.escape: The moment after Fiora Q Lunge and W Riposte are down is your window to engage with Quinn E Vault. If Fiora uses Q to move deeper into the enemy team and you use E, Quinn follows her too, so first check whether Fiora's mobility is down and your allies can follow. If Fiora gets on you to retaliate, use E to knock her back and escape.
Fiora.fight: When Fiora steps up to last-hit, poke briefly with an attack marked by Quinn P Harrier, then retreat. If Fiora gets on you to retaliate, knock her back with Quinn E Vault, but if Fiora W Riposte is still available, first look for an opportunity to bait it out. Engage after Fiora Q Lunge and W Riposte are down, and avoid chasing her too deep.
Fiora.laning: Use your ranged advantage to land a marked attack when Fiora steps forward to last-hit, then quickly back off. Stand opposite the vital on you to limit Fiora's angle to engage, and don't overcommit to chasing after a short trade. Push the wave under Fiora's turret, then use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to rotate to another lane or the enemy jungle.
Fiora.phase: Early on, Quinn can pressure melee Fiora with mark-based poke.
Fiora.teamfight: Quinn doesn't engage from the front; she finishes targets already caught from the side or behind, and saves Quinn E Vault to knock away enemies who get on her and escape. If Fiora R Grand Challenge hits you, stand against a wall to block one side's vital. You can push the opposite side lane and then join the fight, but if your team is about to collapse, rotate early with Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines.
Fiora.watch: Fiora W Riposte blocks Quinn E Vault and counters with a stab; if it blocks an immobilizing effect, it also stuns. Don't rush E while Riposte is available, and move sideways when using it to avoid Riposte's hitbox. Watch Fiora Q Lunge for her attempts to move toward a vital, and if Fiora R Grand Challenge hits you, stand against a wall to block one side's vital.

Gangplank.build: Build armor early in lane against the physical damage from Gangplank Q Parrrley and E Powder Keg. If Gangplank W Remove Scurvy’s healing is blunting your poke, fit Executioner’s Calling between your core items. Resistance can’t mitigate the true damage from Gangplank P Trial by Fire and R Cannon Barrage, so you need enough health to withstand it.
Gangplank.combo: For a short trade, use a Quinn P Harrier-marked attack, an extra attack with Quinn W Heightened Senses’ passive active, then Quinn E Vault to knock him back as you retreat. If Gangplank W Remove Scurvy is down and you have an opening to engage while Gangplank E Powder Keg is unprimed, use Quinn E Vault, an empowered attack immediately after landing, Quinn Q Blinding Assault, then an attack. Immediately consume the mark left by Quinn E Vault to activate Quinn W Heightened Senses’ passive.
Gangplank.escape: Gangplank has no ability to create distance, so look to engage just after he places Gangplank E Powder Keg, when there are no primed kegs nearby. If Gangplank W Remove Scurvy is down, he can’t remove Quinn E Vault’s displacement. Before engaging, check whether Gangplank has Flash and whether your allies can follow up.
Gangplank.fight: Trade briefly just after Gangplank places E Powder Keg, while it is still unprimed. Hit a target marked by Quinn P Harrier to gain Quinn W Heightened Senses’ attack speed and movement speed, land extra attacks, then use Quinn E Vault to knock Gangplank back and disengage when he comes to retaliate. If Gangplank E Powder Keg is primed, back away first. After Gangplank W Remove Scurvy is down, use Quinn E Vault’s displacement to set up a kill.
Gangplank.laning: Repeatedly poke Gangplank with a Quinn P Harrier-marked attack as he steps up to last-hit, then back away. Quinn Q Blinding Assault won’t mark him if it hits a minion first, so cast it when he steps out from behind the minion wave. Push the wave under his turret, then use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to move to another lane or into the enemy jungle.
Gangplank.phase: Early on, Quinn can build a lane advantage with poke from Quinn P Harrier. In the late game, Quinn has less of a role in head-on teamfights, so pressure a side lane and time objective fights around whether Gangplank R Cannon Barrage has been used.
Gangplank.teamfight: Don’t engage from the front; clean up targets already caught from the side or behind. Save Quinn E Vault to knock back nearby enemies and disengage. Even while pushing the opposite side lane, remember that Gangplank R Cannon Barrage can land anywhere, so don’t cross a wide area alone at low health.
Gangplank.watch: If Gangplank E Powder Keg is primed, back away to avoid its explosion and slow. Break the keg yourself from outside the blast radius, and don’t step where two kegs overlap. Gangplank P Trial by Fire and R Cannon Barrage deal true damage, so when low on health, move with Gangplank R Cannon Barrage in mind.

Garen.build: Build armor first against Garen’s main damage from Q Decisive Strike and E Judgment. If Garen P Perseverance heals away your poke, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items. Garen R Demacian Justice’s true damage can’t be reduced by resistance, so account for your total health when judging whether you can withstand it.
Garen.combo: A basic trade is a Quinn P Harrier-marked attack, one or two attacks with Quinn W Heightened Senses’ passive active, then Quinn E Vault to knock him back as you retreat. If Garen Q Decisive Strike is expended and Garen W Courage’s brief shield and tenacity window has passed, take the opening with Quinn E Vault, an empowered attack immediately after landing, Quinn Q Blinding Assault, then an attack.
Garen.escape: Engage after Garen’s empowered attack from Q Decisive Strike has been expended, and delay Quinn E Vault by half a beat if he activates Garen W Courage. Garen has no ability to create distance, but if he Flashes deeper into the enemy team, Quinn E Vault may follow him and leave you in a dangerous spot. Check whether he has Flash and whether your allies can follow before engaging.
Garen.fight: Trade briefly just after Garen uses the empowered attack from Q Decisive Strike on a minion or otherwise expends it. Attack a target marked by Quinn P Harrier to gain Quinn W Heightened Senses’ attack speed and movement speed, then use Quinn E Vault to create distance when Garen approaches. When Garen activates W Courage, don’t use Quinn E Vault immediately; delay it by half a beat.
Garen.laning: Quinn Q Blinding Assault won’t mark Garen if it hits a minion first, so use it when he steps out from behind the minion wave. Pressure him early to limit the time he has to build stacks on Garen W Courage, then push the wave under his turret and use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to create a numbers advantage elsewhere.
Garen.phase: In the late game, Garen W Courage's permanent growth stacks accumulate and Quinn has less of a role in head-on teamfights, so play around side-lane pressure.
Garen.teamfight: Don’t engage from the front; clean up targets already caught from the side or behind. Save Quinn E Vault to knock back enemies who get on you and disengage, and don’t stay in range of Garen E Judgment’s spin for long. If a head-on teamfight looks unfavorable, push the opposite side lane while using Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines and judging whether to join.
Garen.watch: Garen Q Decisive Strike empowers his next attack and silences you, so don’t approach while it’s active. Don’t stay in range of Garen E Judgment’s spin for long; use Quinn E Vault to knock him back and disengage. If you’re below half health, stay outside Garen R Demacian Justice’s range, as it deals true damage based on your missing health.

Gnar.build: Build armor first against Gnar’s main physical damage. Gnar W Hyper / Wallop deals magic damage that armor can’t block and scales with your maximum health, so be wary of stacking health alone. If you can’t use Quinn E Vault to avoid the wall stun from Gnar R GNAR!, consider tenacity first.
Gnar.combo: For a short trade, use a Quinn P Harrier-marked empowered attack, an extra attack with Quinn W Heightened Senses’ attack speed and movement speed, then Quinn E Vault to knock him back as you disengage. For an all-in after Gnar E Hop / Crunch is down, use Quinn E Vault, a mark-empowered attack immediately after landing, Quinn Q Blinding Assault, then an extra attack. Using Quinn E Vault first lets you take advantage of the new mark and Quinn W Heightened Senses on the follow-up attack.
Gnar.escape: Look to engage immediately after Gnar’s mobility ability, Gnar E Hop / Crunch, has been spent. If you use Quinn E Vault while he’s escaping with Gnar E Hop / Crunch, Quinn will follow his movement and land, so confirm his movement before using it. Keep your distance if Mega Gnar R GNAR! could stun you against a wall.
Gnar.fight: As soon as Mini Gnar is marked by P Harrier, consume the mark with an empowered attack and use Quinn W Heightened Senses’ attack speed and movement speed for a short trade. If he approaches to retaliate, use Quinn E Vault to knock him back and retreat. Look for an all-in when Gnar E Hop / Crunch is down, or while Mega Gnar has just reverted to Mini Gnar and can’t transform again yet.
Gnar.laning: Mini Gnar can poke from range too, so dodge the path of Gnar Q Boomerang Throw / Boulder Toss while using P Harrier’s mark on him. Quinn Q Blinding Assault won’t mark Gnar if it hits a minion first, so use it when he steps out from behind the minion wave. Push the wave under his turret, then use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to create a numbers advantage in another lane or the enemy jungle.
Gnar.phase: Early on, Quinn is strong at short trades using Quinn P Harrier’s mark, but Mini Gnar can also poke from range, so watch Gnar’s rage and boomerang path as you fight. Just after Mega Gnar ends and he reverts to Mini Gnar, exploit the window when he can’t transform again. In the mid game, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to pressure side lanes and other lanes; in the late game, prioritize side-lane play over head-on teamfights.
Gnar.teamfight: Avoid standing with your back to a wall or in narrow terrain where Mega Gnar R GNAR! could stun you against a wall. Quinn should clean up targets already caught from the side or behind instead of engaging from the front, and save Quinn E Vault to knock back nearby enemies and disengage. If Mega Gnar has just reverted to Mini Gnar, you can start a fight with your allies while he can’t transform again.
Gnar.watch: Dodge both the outbound and returning paths of Gnar Q Boomerang Throw / Boulder Toss, and move out of the path so Mini Gnar can’t catch his boomerang. Back away as his rage builds and a transformation approaches; don’t take Mega Gnar’s burst head-on. Mega Gnar R GNAR! stuns targets knocked into a wall, so don’t stand with your back to one.

Gwen.build: If Gwen P A Thousand Cuts heals away your poke, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items. Gwen’s high armor can blunt Quinn’s physical damage, so include armor penetration in your build. Build magic resistance first against Gwen’s main magic damage, but avoid the true damage at the center of Gwen Q Snip Snip! by managing your distance and angle.
Gwen.combo: For a short trade, use a Quinn P Harrier-marked attack, land one or two more attacks with Quinn W Heightened Senses’ passive active, then use Quinn E Vault to knock her back and end the trade. If Gwen E Skip 'n Slash is down and you can engage, go in with Quinn E Vault, then immediately after landing use a mark-empowered attack, Quinn Q Blinding Assault, and an attack. If Gwen W Hallowed Mist is active, you can’t target her from outside the mist, so delay your engage.
Gwen.escape: The moment after you force Gwen to use Gwen E Skip 'n Slash is an opportunity to go in with Quinn E Vault. If Gwen E Skip 'n Slash is still available when you engage with Quinn E Vault, you may follow Gwen's movement and land in a dangerous position, so check whether she has used it first. Save Quinn E Vault to knock Gwen back and disengage when she approaches to retaliate.
Gwen.fight: Briefly poke Gwen with a Quinn P Harrier-marked attack as she steps up to last-hit, then use the attack speed and movement speed from Quinn W Heightened Senses to retreat. If Gwen approaches to retaliate, use Quinn E Vault to knock her back.
Gwen.laning: Don’t consume Quinn P Harrier’s mark on a minion; save it to poke Gwen when she steps up to last-hit. Quinn Q Blinding Assault won’t mark Gwen if it hits a minion first, so use it when she steps outside the minion line. Push the wave under Gwen’s turret, then use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to move to another lane or into the enemy jungle.
Gwen.phase: Early on, Quinn can take control with ranged mark poke and short trades before Gwen builds stacks on Q Snip Snip! Quinn peaks in the mid game after her first core item and has less of a role in front-to-back teamfights late, so keep up the side-lane pressure.
Gwen.teamfight: Don’t engage from the front; clean up targets already caught from the side or behind. Keep enough distance to avoid the center of Gwen Q Snip Snip!, and save Quinn E Vault to knock back nearby enemies and disengage. If a front-to-back teamfight looks unfavorable, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines’ movement speed to push the opposite side lane and choose when to join.
Gwen.watch: The center of Gwen Q Snip Snip! deals true damage, so move to the side to avoid it when Gwen approaches. While Gwen W Hallowed Mist is active, you can’t target her from outside the mist, so wait for it to end. Keep your distance to avoid the slow and maximum-health-based damage from Gwen R Needlework.

Illaoi.build: If Illaoi sustains through trades with Illaoi P Prophet of an Elder God, fit Executioner’s Calling between your core items to apply Grievous Wounds. Build armor first against Illaoi’s main damage. Illaoi W Harsh Lesson deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid stacking health alone.
Illaoi.combo: For a short trade, use a Quinn P Harrier-marked attack to gain Quinn W Heightened Senses’ attack speed and movement speed, land one or two attacks, then use Quinn E Vault to knock her back and end the trade. After Illaoi W Harsh Lesson is down, engage with Quinn E Vault, an empowered attack, Quinn Q Blinding Assault, then an attack. Use Quinn E Vault first so you can land the marked attack immediately after landing.
Illaoi.escape: Dodge Illaoi E Test of Spirit, then go in with Quinn E Vault just after Illaoi W Harsh Lesson is down. If you use Quinn E Vault while Illaoi is moving deeper into enemy territory with Illaoi W Harsh Lesson, Quinn will follow, so check where you’ll land first. If Illaoi retaliates, use Quinn E Vault to knock her back and disengage.
Illaoi.fight: Briefly poke Illaoi with a Quinn P Harrier-marked attack as she steps up to last-hit, then back away. If you dodge Illaoi E Test of Spirit or just after she uses Illaoi W Harsh Lesson, you have an opportunity to close the distance and fight. Don’t take an extended fight while Illaoi R Leap of Faith is active.
Illaoi.laning: Keep the wave away from walls and last-hit outside Illaoi E Test of Spirit’s range. When Illaoi steps out from behind the minion wave, hit her with Quinn Q Blinding Assault to apply a mark, then repeat short attack trades. After pushing the lane, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to move to another lane or into the enemy jungle.
Illaoi.phase: Early on, Quinn can pressure Illaoi with ranged mark poke. Quinn is strong in the mid game after her first core item, so push the lane and use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to create a numbers advantage elsewhere. In the late game, Quinn has less of a role in front-to-back teamfights, so maintain pressure through side lanes.
Illaoi.teamfight: Don’t group up in front of Illaoi R Leap of Faith, and don’t fight near her tentacles. Quinn should clean up only targets already caught from the side or behind, and save Quinn E Vault as an escape. If your allies can hold, push the opposite side lane; if the fight is about to collapse, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to join early.
Illaoi.watch: Dodge Illaoi E Test of Spirit, and if it hits, first decide whether you can fight. When Illaoi R Leap of Faith is active, don’t fight near her tentacles; create distance for its duration. Illaoi W Harsh Lesson dashes and deals damage based on your maximum health, so check whether she has used it before engaging.

Irelia.build: If Irelia Q Bladesurge’s healing makes your poke ineffective, fit Executioner’s Calling between your core items. The information provided isn’t enough to determine which item to buy first or which resistance to build.
Irelia.combo: For a short trade, use a Quinn P Harrier-marked attack to gain Quinn W Heightened Senses’ attack speed and movement speed, land one or two more attacks, then use Quinn E Vault to knock her back and disengage. If you can finish the fight by engaging just after Irelia uses Q Bladesurge, use Quinn E Vault, a mark-empowered attack, Quinn Q Blinding Assault, then an attack. Cast Quinn Q Blinding Assault when you have a clear line so it won’t hit a minion first.
Irelia.escape: Use Quinn E Vault to engage just after Irelia uses Q Bladesurge. If Irelia uses Q Bladesurge to move deeper into enemy territory, Quinn E Vault will follow her, so don’t engage in that direction. Be careful to avoid the stun from Irelia E Flawless Duet.
Irelia.fight: Briefly poke Irelia with a Quinn P Harrier-marked attack as she steps up to last-hit. Just after Irelia uses Q Bladesurge is an opportunity to engage, but before following up with Quinn E Vault, check Irelia’s movement direction and whether your allies can follow.
Irelia.laning: Don’t leave a low-health minion between you and Irelia. Push the wave under the enemy turret, then use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to join your allies elsewhere.
Irelia.phase: In the late game, Quinn has less of a role in front-to-back teamfights, so use side-lane pressure.
Irelia.teamfight: Don’t engage from the front; prioritize cleaning up Irelia when she’s already caught from the side or behind. Save Quinn E Vault to knock back nearby enemies and disengage, and avoid getting caught by Irelia R Vanguard’s Edge and E Flawless Duet. If your allies can hold, push the opposite side lane; if the fight is about to collapse, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to join early.
Irelia.watch: Irelia Q Bladesurge can chain toward you by dashing through low-health minions, so create distance when minions are close to dying. Watch out for the stun from Irelia E Flawless Duet, and if you’re trapped inside Irelia R Vanguard’s Edge, wait for the blades to disappear.

Jax.build: Jax’s damage relies on basic attacks and attack speed, so consider an item that reduces attack speed first. Jax Q Leap Strike deals physical damage, while Jax W Empower and E Counter Strike deal magic damage, so don’t focus your resistances on just one type.
Jax.combo: If you can engage after Jax Q Leap Strike and E Counter Strike are down, use Quinn E Vault, a Quinn P Harrier-marked empowered attack, Quinn Q Blinding Assault, then an attack. Quinn Q Blinding Assault won’t mark Jax if it hits a minion first, so use it when you have a clear line.
Jax.escape: Don’t use Quinn E Vault just because you see Jax activate E Counter Strike. The opportunity to engage with Quinn E Vault comes after both Jax Q Leap Strike and E Counter Strike are down. If Jax can use his mobility to escape deeper into enemy territory, first check where you’ll land if you follow.
Jax.fight: Briefly poke Jax with a Quinn P Harrier-marked attack as he steps up to last-hit, then use the movement speed from Quinn W Heightened Senses to retreat. If Jax E Counter Strike is active, stop basic attacking; trade again after it ends.
Jax.laning: Keep your distance while watching the position of allied minions Jax could use as a springboard for Q Leap Strike. Push the wave, then use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to create a numbers advantage elsewhere.
Jax.phase: In the late game, Quinn has less of a role in front-to-back teamfights, so push side lanes and choose when to join.
Jax.teamfight: If Jax activates E Counter Strike and jumps in, don’t group up; move outside its stun range. Quinn should clean up targets already caught from the side, and save Quinn E Vault to knock back nearby enemies and disengage.
Jax.watch: When Jax E Counter Strike is active, stop basic attacking and move outside its stun range. Jax Q Leap Strike can use minions as a springboard, so don’t stand beside your allied minion wave and keep track of his engage range.

Jayce.build: If you need defense, build magic resistance first against the damage from Jayce W Lightning Field and E Thundering Blow. Magic resistance won’t block the physical damage from Jayce Q Shock Blast, and Jayce R Mercury Cannon / Mercury Hammer can reduce your resistances. Get movement speed to leave telegraphed attack areas, and avoid stacking health alone because of damage based on maximum health.
Jayce.combo: For a short trade, use a Quinn P Harrier-marked empowered attack, an extra attack with Quinn W Heightened Senses active, then Quinn E Vault to knock him back as you disengage. If Jayce Q To the Skies! is down and you can engage safely, go in with Quinn E Vault, then follow up immediately after landing with an empowered attack, Quinn Q Blinding Assault, and an extra attack.
Jayce.escape: Just after Jayce Q To the Skies! is down is your window to engage with Quinn E Vault. Before going in, consider the knockback from Jayce E Thundering Blow and where you’ll land; don’t follow Jayce when he has moved deeper into enemy territory.
Jayce.fight: When Quinn P Harrier marks Jayce, use an empowered attack to gain Quinn W Heightened Senses’ attack speed and movement speed for a short trade. Just after Jayce Q To the Skies! is down, you have an opportunity to close the distance with Quinn E Vault, but check your engage position first, as Quinn will follow and land there if Jayce moves deeper into enemy territory.
Jayce.laning: When Jayce is holding the cannon, farm by moving sideways to dodge the line of Jayce Q Shock Blast. Use Quinn Q Blinding Assault when Jayce steps out from behind the minion wave so it won’t hit a minion first. After pushing the wave, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to affect another lane, but if you fell behind early, farm defensively instead of forcing a comeback.
Jayce.phase: In the late game, focus on side-lane pressure and choosing when to join instead of front-to-back teamfights.
Jayce.teamfight: Don’t engage from the front; clean up targets already caught from the side or behind. Look for an opportunity to engage after Jayce Q To the Skies! is down, but save Quinn E Vault so you can knock back an approaching enemy and disengage. If your allies can hold, push the opposite side lane; if the fight is about to collapse, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to join early.
Jayce.watch: When Jayce places E Acceleration Gate, expect Jayce Q Shock Blast and move sideways out of its line. When Jayce holds the hammer, watch out for the leap from Jayce Q To the Skies! and the knockback from Jayce E Thundering Blow.

Kayle.build: Quinn’s main physical damage works well against Kayle’s low armor, so focus on early pressure. If the healing from Kayle W Celestial Blessing dulls your poke, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. If you build armor, you still won’t stop Kayle’s magic damage, so choose magic resistance and dodge Kayle Q Radiant Blast.
Kayle.combo: For a short trade, basic attack Kayle while she has the Quinn P Harrier mark, then use the attack speed and movement speed from Quinn W Heightened Senses to land one or two more attacks before ending with Quinn E Vault to knock her back. When you have a clear opening, apply the mark with Quinn E Vault, then attack in this order: empowered attack immediately after landing → Quinn Q Blinding Assault → basic attack. If Kayle R Divine Judgment activates, stop dealing damage and attack again after the invulnerability ends.
Kayle.escape: Kayle has no mobility spell, so look for an opening to go in with Quinn E Vault as soon as Kayle Q Radiant Blast misses and you avoid the slow. Even when Kayle W Celestial Blessing grants movement speed, she has no mobility spell to create distance. However, if Kayle Flashes toward the enemy team, Quinn E Vault can follow and land you in danger, so check before engaging.
Kayle.fight: After dodging Kayle Q Radiant Blast, look for an opening to go in with Quinn E Vault. If Kayle R Divine Judgment is available, hold your damage during the invulnerability and use Quinn E Vault’s forced movement to run out the duration.
Kayle.laning: When Kayle steps forward to last-hit, land a Quinn P Harrier-marked basic attack and back off to pressure her CS and experience. Quinn Q Blinding Assault won’t mark Kayle if it hits a minion first, so use it when Kayle steps outside the minion line.
Kayle.teamfight: Find a path to Kayle from the side or out of vision instead of engaging from the front. Time your approach with your allies’ crowd control, then focus damage after Kayle R Divine Judgment’s invulnerability ends. After engaging, use Quinn E Vault to knock away enemies who get on you and escape, or use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to pressure the opposite side lane instead of fighting head-on.
Kayle.watch: Kayle Q Radiant Blast slows and reduces armor and magic resistance, so avoid being hit directly. Kayle E Starfire Spellblade deals more damage based on missing health, so be especially careful at low health. Don’t commit damage while Kayle R Divine Judgment is active; attack again once the invulnerability ends.

Malphite.build: Build magic resistance first against the damage from Malphite Q Seismic Shard, E Ground Slam, and R Unstoppable Force. Quinn’s main physical damage is easily blocked by Malphite’s high armor, so consider armor penetration or damage that armor can’t mitigate when increasing your damage.
Malphite.combo: If you can engage when Malphite R Unstoppable Force is down, go in with Quinn E Vault, use an empowered basic attack on the marked target immediately after landing, then follow with Quinn Q Blinding Assault and basic attacks. Quinn Q Blinding Assault won’t leave a mark on Malphite if it hits a minion first, so use it when he steps outside the minion line.
Malphite.escape: If you engage with Quinn E Vault just before Malphite uses R Unstoppable Force, Quinn may follow the dash and land in danger, so first check whether he’ll use it and whether your allies can follow.
Malphite.fight: Trade briefly when you can break Malphite P Granite Shield and damage his actual health. Use a Quinn P Harrier-marked basic attack to gain the attack speed and movement speed from Quinn W Heightened Senses, land one or two more attacks, then knock Malphite back with Quinn E Vault and disengage if he closes in to retaliate. Don’t stay close and keep attacking before Malphite E Ground Slam is down.
Malphite.laning: Poke at short intervals to keep Malphite P Granite Shield from regenerating, but don’t stay within range of Malphite Q Seismic Shard for long. Push the wave into the enemy turret, then use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to join another lane or the enemy jungle.
Malphite.phase: Mid game after your first core item is Quinn’s strongest period, so push the lane and use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to create a numbers advantage elsewhere.
Malphite.teamfight: Spread out from your allies so Malphite R Unstoppable Force can’t knock up several of you. If you can’t see him, don’t rush an engage. Counterattack as soon as Malphite R Unstoppable Force is down, with Quinn approaching from the side or behind to finish targets who are already caught. Save Quinn E Vault to knock away enemies who get on you and escape.
Malphite.watch: Malphite Q Seismic Shard slows and steals movement speed, so don’t start a trade right after it hits you. Malphite E Ground Slam reduces attack speed and cuts Quinn’s basic attack damage output, so wait outside its area and attack after it’s down. Malphite R Unstoppable Force can’t be interrupted with Quinn E Vault, so when you can’t see him, don’t give him an engage angle near bushes or walls.

Nasus.build: Build armor first against Nasus’s main damage from Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Armor won’t block damage from Nasus E Spirit Fire or Nasus R Fury of the Sands, so getting out of Nasus E Spirit Fire’s area is the priority.
Nasus.combo: For a short trade while Nasus has the Quinn P Harrier mark, use an empowered basic attack to gain the attack speed and movement speed from Quinn W Heightened Senses, land one or two more attacks, then end with Quinn E Vault to knock him back. If Nasus W Wither is down and you have an opening to engage, attack in this order: Quinn E Vault → empowered attack on the mark → Quinn Q Blinding Assault → basic attack.
Nasus.escape: It’s safer to engage while Nasus W Wither is down. Nasus has no way to create distance except Flash, but if he Flashes toward your team, Quinn E Vault can follow and land you in danger, so check your engage direction.
Nasus.fight: Early on, when Nasus steps up to last-hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike, land a Quinn P Harrier-marked basic attack and briefly back off.
Nasus.laning: Don’t blindly push the early lane into Nasus’s turret and let him comfortably stack Nasus Q Siphoning Strike with last-hits. Poke Nasus when he steps up to last-hit in a wave pushing toward you, and call your jungler for a gank. Later, if you can push the wave in, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to move to another lane.
Nasus.phase: Quinn has less impact in front-to-back teamfights later, so use side-lane pressure.
Nasus.teamfight: Keep your distance so Nasus W Wither doesn’t catch you alone, and kite Nasus as you fight back. Instead of engaging from the front, approach from the side to finish targets who are already caught, and save Quinn E Vault as an escape tool to knock away enemies who get on you. If your allies can hold, push the opposite side lane; if the fight is about to collapse, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to join early.
Nasus.watch: Nasus W Wither reduces Quinn’s movement and attack speed, making it harder to poke with basic attacks and escape. Don’t stay within Nasus’s range alone for long. If Nasus R Fury of the Sands is active, avoid fighting unless you clearly have the numbers or damage advantage.

Ornn.combo: Start a short trade with a Quinn P Harrier-marked basic attack, land one or two more attacks empowered by Quinn W Heightened Senses’ passive, then end with Quinn E Vault to knock Ornn back. When you have an opening to engage, go in with Quinn E Vault, use a basic attack on the marked target immediately after landing, then follow with Quinn Q Blinding Assault and basic attacks.
Ornn.escape: Don’t engage just because Ornn E Searing Charge is down; check whether Ornn R Call of the Forge God is still available too. Close the distance with Quinn E Vault when both mobility spells are down and the Brittle effect from Ornn W Bellows Breath has ended. If Ornn can escape deeper into the enemy team with a mobility spell, Quinn E Vault follows and lands you in danger, so delay your engage.
Ornn.fight: When Ornn steps up to last-hit, briefly poke with a basic attack marked by Quinn P Harrier. Use the attack speed and movement speed from Quinn W Heightened Senses to land more attacks, then back off. If Ornn closes in to retaliate, knock him back with Quinn E Vault, angling it so you don’t land near a pillar from Ornn Q Volcanic Rupture or a wall.
Ornn.laning: Early on, chip away at melee Ornn’s health with a Quinn P Harrier-marked basic attack whenever he steps up to last-hit. Use Quinn Q Blinding Assault when minions don’t block its path, and attack Ornn to interrupt him if he tries to craft items in lane. Push the wave into Ornn’s turret, then use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to join another lane or the enemy jungle.
Ornn.phase: Early on, Quinn can pressure melee Ornn with mark pokes. Quinn has less impact in front-to-back teamfights later, so push and play through the side lane.
Ornn.teamfight: Don’t engage from the front; approach from the side or behind to finish targets who are already caught. Save Quinn E Vault to knock away enemies who get on you and escape, and avoid the line between Ornn R Call of the Forge God’s summoned ram and Ornn. You can join with Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines if you’re pushing the opposite side lane, but join early if your allies are about to collapse.
Ornn.watch: Near a pillar from Ornn Q Volcanic Rupture, Ornn E Searing Charge can knock you up, so move away from the pillar and walls into open space. If you’re hit by the final burst of Ornn W Bellows Breath, don’t move forward; keep your distance until Brittle ends. Avoid the line between Ornn R Call of the Forge God’s summoned ram and Ornn, and watch for the return path as well.

Pantheon.build: Build armor first against Pantheon’s main damage. Pantheon tends to have high armor, so add penetration to help Quinn’s physical damage get through. Pantheon W Shield Vault deals damage based on maximum health, so avoid relying on stacking health alone.
Pantheon.combo: For a short trade, use a basic attack on a Quinn P Harrier-marked target to activate the attack speed and movement speed increase from Quinn W Heightened Senses, add one or two more basic attacks, then retreat with Quinn E Vault. If Pantheon W Shield Vault and Pantheon R Grand Starfall have been used and you can engage, attack in this order: Quinn E Vault → basic attack on a marked target immediately after landing → Quinn Q Blinding Assault → basic attack. Wait to attack or change your angle while Pantheon E Aegis Assault blocks the front.
Pantheon.escape: The window to engage with Quinn E Vault opens after Pantheon W Shield Vault has been used. Check whether Pantheon R Grand Starfall has also been used before engaging. Quinn E Vault follows its target’s movement, so if Pantheon still has a mobility ability available, you may land inside the enemy team.
Pantheon.fight: When Pantheon steps up to last-hit, briefly harass him with a basic attack on a Quinn P Harrier-marked target, then retreat. If he closes in to retaliate, knock him back with Quinn E Vault and create distance. Look to engage after Pantheon W Shield Vault and Pantheon R Grand Starfall have been used.
Pantheon.laning: Avoid extended trades with Pantheon early, and stand behind minions against Pantheon Q Comet Spear. Quinn Q Blinding Assault won’t mark Pantheon if it hits a minion first, so cast it when he steps outside the minion line. After shoving the wave in, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to move to another lane or the enemy jungle.
Pantheon.phase: Pantheon has less impact late, but Quinn is also weaker in front-to-back teamfights, so use side-lane pressure.
Pantheon.teamfight: Don’t engage from the front; clean up only targets who are already caught from the flank or behind. Save Quinn E Vault to knock back a Pantheon who closes in and escape. If you’re pushing the opposite side lane and your team is about to collapse, join early with Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines.
Pantheon.watch: Pantheon W Shield Vault stuns a targeted enemy, so it’s important to stay out of its range. Pantheon E Aegis Assault blocks damage from the direction he faces, so don’t unload attacks from the front; wait for it to end or angle in from the side. When you see the landing warning for Pantheon R Grand Starfall, walk out of its landing area.

Poppy.build: Build armor first against Poppy’s main damage from Poppy Q Hammer Shock, Poppy E Heroic Charge, and Poppy R Keeper’s Verdict. Don’t spend extra resources on magic resistance for Poppy alone, and avoid stacking large amounts of health alone because Poppy Q Hammer Shock deals damage based on maximum health.
Poppy.combo: During the window after Poppy W Steadfast Presence ends and Poppy E Heroic Charge has been used, attack in this order: Quinn E Vault → empowered basic attack on a marked target → Quinn Q Blinding Assault → basic attack. Quinn E Vault applies a mark, so use a basic attack immediately after landing to also activate Quinn W Heightened Senses’ passive. If Poppy moves, Quinn E Vault follows her, so first check the landing spot and whether your team can follow up.
Poppy.escape: The window to close in opens just after you bait Poppy E Heroic Charge, but wait to engage with Quinn E Vault if Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active. Once Poppy W Steadfast Presence ends and Poppy E Heroic Charge has been used, engage from a direction that avoids landing near a wall.
Poppy.fight: When Poppy steps up to last-hit, briefly harass her with a basic attack on a Quinn P Harrier-marked target, then add more basic attacks using the attack speed and movement speed from Quinn W Heightened Senses and retreat. If Poppy closes in to retaliate, make sure Poppy W Steadfast Presence has ended, then knock her back with Quinn E Vault and disengage. Poppy’s armor increases even when she’s low, so only go deep when you can finish her for certain.
Poppy.laning: Use Quinn’s range to land a marked basic attack whenever Poppy steps up to last-hit, then briefly retreat. Quinn Q Blinding Assault won’t mark Poppy if it hits a minion first, so cast it when she steps outside the minion line. Don’t stand with a wall behind you, and look for a path that lets you safely step on Poppy P Iron Ambassador’s shield before she can pick it up when it drops.
Poppy.phase: Quinn has a smaller role in front-to-back teamfights late, so maintain your impact through side-lane pressure.
Poppy.teamfight: Don’t engage from the front; clean up only targets who are already caught from the flank or behind. Save Quinn E Vault to knock back enemies who close in and escape after Poppy W Steadfast Presence ends. When pushing the opposite side lane, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to choose when to join, but join early if your team is about to collapse.
Poppy.watch: If you dash with Quinn E Vault while Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active, the dash will be stopped and you’ll briefly be unable to use movement abilities, so wait for it to end. Poppy E Heroic Charge stuns you if it knocks you into a wall, so don’t stand with your back to a wall; stand in open space. If you’re hit by Poppy Q Hammer Shock, leave the remaining zone immediately; if Poppy charges Poppy R Keeper’s Verdict, move sideways out of its front-facing path.

Renekton.build: If Renekton Q Cull the Meek’s healing makes your harass ineffective, fit Executioner’s Calling between your core items. Build armor first against Renekton’s main damage. However, the empowered recast of Renekton E Slice and Dice reduces armor, so focus on positioning to avoid the dash rather than stacking more armor.
Renekton.combo: For a short trade, use a basic attack on a Quinn P Harrier-marked target to gain the attack speed and movement speed increase from Quinn W Heightened Senses, add one or two more basic attacks, then knock Renekton back with Quinn E Vault to end the trade. When Renekton E Slice and Dice and Renekton W Ruthless Predator are down and you can all-in, engage with Quinn E Vault, then use a basic attack on the marked target immediately after landing, followed by Quinn Q Blinding Assault and basic attacks.
Renekton.escape: Engage with Quinn E Vault after Renekton has used Renekton E Slice and Dice to disengage and Renekton W Ruthless Predator’s stun is down. If Renekton can use a mobility ability to escape deeper into the enemy team, Quinn E Vault may follow and land you in a dangerous spot, so check whether your team can follow before engaging.
Renekton.fight: When Renekton’s Fury bar is empty, briefly harass him with a basic attack on a Quinn P Harrier-marked target. If he closes in to retaliate, knock him back with Quinn E Vault and retreat. Pressure him again immediately after he has fully spent Renekton Q Cull the Meek, Renekton W Ruthless Predator, and Renekton E Slice and Dice.
Renekton.laning: Quinn Q Blinding Assault won’t mark a champion if it hits a minion first, so cast it when Renekton steps outside the minion line. After pushing the wave under the enemy turret, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to create a numbers advantage in another lane or the enemy jungle.
Renekton.phase: Don’t fight while Renekton R Dominus is active, and avoid giving up a kill while making use of Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines and Quinn’s mid-game strength after her first core item. Quinn has a smaller role in front-to-back teamfights late, so pressure the side lanes.
Renekton.teamfight: Don’t engage from the front; clean up targets who are already caught from the flank or behind. Save Quinn E Vault to knock back enemies who close in and escape. Push the opposite side lane if your team can hold; if the fight is about to collapse, join early with Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines.
Renekton.watch: If Renekton P Reign of Anger is above or just below half, he can stun you with empowered Renekton W Ruthless Predator, so stay out of its range. Renekton E Slice and Dice unlocks a second dash if the first hits a unit, so don’t stand among or behind a group of minions.

Riven.build: Riven deals physical damage, so build armor first. If Riven gets ahead, move defensive items earlier in your build, and get enough health to avoid being finished off by Riven R Blade of the Exile.
Riven.combo: For a safe trade, use a basic attack on a Quinn P Harrier-marked target to gain the attack speed and movement speed increase from Quinn W Heightened Senses, add one or two more basic attacks, then knock Riven back with Quinn E Vault to end the trade. If Riven Q Broken Wings has been fully spent and Riven E Valor is also down, allowing you to engage, attack in this order: Quinn E Vault → empowered basic attack on a marked target → Quinn Q Blinding Assault → basic attack. Cast Quinn Q Blinding Assault when Riven is outside the minion line so it doesn’t hit a minion first.
Riven.escape: The window for Quinn to engage opens when Riven Q Broken Wings has been fully spent and Riven E Valor is also down. If Riven still has a mobility ability available, Quinn E Vault may follow her and land you in a dangerous spot, so delay your engage. If Riven closes in and starts her combo, use Quinn E Vault to knock her back.
Riven.fight: When Riven steps up to last-hit, briefly harass her with a basic attack on a Quinn P Harrier-marked target. If she closes in to retaliate, knock her back with Quinn E Vault and retreat. Look to engage after Riven Q Broken Wings has been fully spent and Riven E Valor is also down.
Riven.laning: Early on, use Quinn’s ranged harass to chip away at Riven whenever she steps up to last-hit. If she uses Riven Q Broken Wings to clear minions, that’s your chance to retaliate. After pushing the wave under the enemy turret, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to join another lane or the enemy jungle.
Riven.phase: Early on, Quinn can pressure Riven with mark-based harass. Quinn has a smaller role in frontal teamfights late, so use side-lane pressure.
Riven.teamfight: Don’t engage from the front where Riven is; clean up only targets who are already caught from the flank or behind. Save Quinn E Vault to knock Riven back and escape if she closes in. Push the opposite side lane if your team can hold; if the fight is about to collapse, join early with Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines.
Riven.watch: Riven Q Broken Wings closes distance with consecutive dashes and a knock-up, so retreat when you see the first dash. Use Quinn E Vault to knock Riven back as soon as she closes in, so she can’t stun you with Riven W Ki Burst and continue her combo. When Riven R Blade of the Exile is active, her attack damage and range increase, and the finishing damage grows as more health is missing, so create distance until it ends.

Rumble.build: If you need a defensive item, consider magic resistance first. Rumble P Junkyard Titan and Rumble Q Flamespitter deal damage based on maximum health, so avoid relying on stacking health alone.
Rumble.combo: For a short trade, use a basic attack on a Quinn P Harrier-marked target to gain the attack speed and movement speed increase from Quinn W Heightened Senses, add one or two more basic attacks, then knock Rumble back with Quinn E Vault to end the trade. When you engage, attack in this order: Quinn E Vault → empowered basic attack immediately after landing → Quinn Q Blinding Assault → basic attack. Use the engage combo after the shield from Rumble W Scrap Shield disappears.
Rumble.escape: If you’re hit by the first Rumble E Electro Harpoon, use Quinn E Vault to create distance before the second one arrives. Look to engage after Rumble has used Rumble W Scrap Shield and his escape options are down, as long as you aren’t in a situation where the harpoon forces you to retreat. Rumble has no mobility ability, but if you use Quinn E Vault to engage, you can’t use it to knock him back and escape, so watch your landing spot.
Rumble.fight: Briefly harass from outside Rumble Q Flamespitter’s range with a basic attack on a Quinn P Harrier-marked target, and knock Rumble back with Quinn E Vault and retreat if he tries to close in. If Rumble activates Rumble W Scrap Shield, delay your burst until the shield disappears. Once he has also used Rumble W Scrap Shield, you may have an opening to close in with Quinn E Vault.
Rumble.laning: When Rumble steps forward to last-hit, hit him with a basic attack on a Quinn P Harrier-marked target and retreat immediately. Cast Quinn Q Blinding Assault when Rumble steps outside the minion line so it doesn’t hit a minion first. After pushing the wave under the enemy turret, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to move to another lane or the enemy jungle.
Rumble.phase: Early on, Quinn uses mark-based harass to reduce the time Rumble can stay close and seeks a lane advantage. Quinn has a smaller role in frontal teamfights late, so keep up side-lane pressure.
Rumble.teamfight: Don’t engage from the front; clean up targets who are already caught from the flank or behind. Save Quinn E Vault to knock back enemies who close in and escape, and make sure you don’t land in the middle of the enemy team when engaging toward Rumble. Push the opposite side lane if your team can hold; if the fight is about to collapse, join early with Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines.
Rumble.watch: Rumble Q Flamespitter is dangerous while you’re close, so create distance if Rumble walks in. If you’re hit by the first Rumble E Electro Harpoon, retreat or use Quinn E Vault before the second one arrives. Watch out for the slow from Rumble R The Equalizer as well.

Sett.build: Build armor first, considering the damage from Sett P Pit Grit and Sett Q Knuckle Down’s basic attacks. Resistances don’t work against the true damage at the center of Sett W Haymaker, so focus on positioning to avoid the center rather than stacking health alone.
Sett.combo: For a short trade, use a basic attack on a Quinn P Harrier-marked target → one or two basic attacks empowered by Quinn W Heightened Senses’ passive → knock Sett back with Quinn E Vault and retreat. When Sett R The Show Stopper has been used and you can engage, follow Quinn E Vault → empowered basic attack immediately after landing → Quinn Q Blinding Assault → basic attack. Create distance again after dealing damage, as Sett W Haymaker’s counterattack may become stronger.
Sett.escape: Before engaging, check whether your position could let Sett E Facebreaker stun you. If Sett R The Show Stopper is available, Quinn E Vault may follow Sett deeper into the enemy team, so decide carefully whether to engage.
Sett.fight: When Sett steps up to last-hit, briefly harass him with a basic attack on a Quinn P Harrier-marked target, then retreat using the attack speed and movement speed from Quinn W Heightened Senses. Create distance first if Sett walks in, and knock him back with Quinn E Vault once he closes in. Stop trading right after Sett W Haymaker becomes stronger.
Sett.laning: Stay at range and repeat mark-based harass whenever Sett goes to last-hit. Quinn Q Blinding Assault won’t mark Sett if it hits a minion first, so cast it when he steps outside the minion line. After pushing the wave under Sett’s turret, use Quinn R Behind Enemy Lines to affect another lane or the enemy jungle.
Sett.phase: Quinn has a smaller role in frontal teamfights late, so use side-lane pressure.
